question: A production agent uses 45 different tools across long-running conversations. The team identifies three separate cost sources: tool schema definitions consuming context on every request even when most tools go unused that turn, many small sequential tool calls each leaving a tool_result in history, and the same stable tool definitions being resent and re-priced identically on every request. Which changes directly address these three sources?
options: A) Switch to a model with a 1M-token context window without changing which tools are registered
B) Apply prompt caching to the stable tool definitions so repeated requests pay the discounted cache-read rate
C) Increase max_tokens on every request so more of the response budget is available for tool output
D) Manually shorten tool names to save a few characters per schema across the toolset
E) Use programmatic tool calling so chains of tool calls run as a single script instead of many roundtrips
F) Enable the tool search tool so schemas load on demand instead of being sent upfront
correct_answers: B) Apply prompt caching to the stable tool definitions so repeated requests pay the discounted cache-read rate
E) Use programmatic tool calling so chains of tool calls run as a single script instead of many roundtrips
F) Enable the tool search tool so schemas load on demand instead of being sent upfront
explanations: Incorrect. A larger context window gives more headroom but does not reduce the underlying token cost of the toolset or address any of the three described cost sources.
Correct. Prompt caching does not shrink the token count of tool definitions but cuts what repeated, stable definitions cost on subsequent requests via the discounted cache-read rate.
Incorrect. max_tokens controls the ceiling on generated output length and has no effect on how much context tool definitions or tool_result history consume.
Incorrect. Shortening tool names yields negligible savings and is not a documented strategy for managing tool-related context cost compared to the other approaches.
Correct. Programmatic tool calling collapses chains of tool calls into a single executed script, so intermediate tool_result blocks never enter the conversation history.
Correct. Tool search keeps tool definitions out of the context window until Claude requests them, directly reducing the baseline cost of unused schemas loaded upfront.
